subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Does the supported Gateway threat model require `admin-http-rpc` to reject browser-originated cross-site requests in trusted-proxy or auth-none private-ingress modes, and can a current browser request actually reach a mutating method with ambient authority?
rationale: Token/password modes require explicit bearer credentials, but trusted-proxy and auth-none deployments may have ingress-specific ambient authority; only the security owners can confirm the intended browser boundary and supported ingress contract.

options.title: Validate each auth mode first
options.body: Reproduce browser-originated requests across all supported HTTP auth modes, then add route-level Origin or Fetch Metadata enforcement only where ambient authorization creates a demonstrated mutation path.

options.title: Reject every browser Origin
options.body: Fail all admin HTTP RPC requests carrying an unapproved Origin, accepting the compatibility impact for browser-based or unusual proxy automation.

options.title: Document private-ingress responsibility
options.body: Keep the existing authenticated/private-ingress contract unchanged if no supported auth mode permits a cross-site browser mutation without explicit operator credentials.

recommendation.title: Validate each auth mode first
recommendation.body: Reproduce browser-originated requests across all supported HTTP auth modes, then add route-level Origin or Fetch Metadata enforcement only where ambient authorization creates a demonstrated mutation path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current history connects this person most strongly to both ACP security hardening and Gateway control-boundary work.
